feeds.arrives: One scheme's answer to one claim: Money's reference for the claim, whether it was paid, part-paid or rejected, what was paid in cents, and when the scheme decided.

whileAbsent.unchanged: No claim is sent and no answer arrives. A claim is drafted by the doctor who signed the review, agreed to by the patient, and stops at "Not submitted: no switching partner is connected." That is correct and this file does not change it.

accepts.why: Money's own claim reference, which the switching house was sent with the claim. A scheme's own claim number is not the key: an answer matched on it cannot be matched at all if the switching house is changed.
paid, part-paid or rejected, as claim.decided@1 carries it. A code rather than words, because a scheme's words about why it did not pay are where a diagnosis is repeated back.
What the scheme paid, in whole cents. Nought for a rejection, and never more than the claim asked for, which is reconciled rather than believed.
ZAR, stated rather than assumed.
When the scheme decided, with an offset, so a patient's statement says the day her claim was answered rather than the day the answer was delivered.

beforeSwitchOn.must: A claims switching house is contracted, and the contract names the schemes it reaches, where a claim and its answer are kept and for how long.
beforeSwitchOn.why: A claim tells a scheme that a person was seen, when and for what. Who carries it, and where they keep it, is the first thing a patient is owed before she agrees to send one.

beforeSwitchOn.must: A licensed tariff code set and an ICD-10 code set are adopted with the switching house, and packages/catalog/claims.json codeSets.adopted names them.
beforeSwitchOn.why: A claim coded from memory, from a list found somewhere or from a service's name is a claim coded by nobody. packages/catalog/claims.json adopts none today.

beforeSwitchOn.must: A signed data protection impact assessment covers health information sent to a medical scheme through a switching house.
beforeSwitchOn.why: A claim is identifiable health information leaving MyThuso, which is the processing docs/governance names a DPIA for, and none is signed.

neverAccepts.refusal: A claim response may not carry a diagnosis or why a service was needed.
neverAccepts.why: Money faces payers and never holds why somebody was seen. A scheme's answer that repeats the diagnosis back would put it in the one engine built never to hold it.

neverAccepts.refusal: A claim response may not carry a scheme membership number.
neverAccepts.why: A membership number joins a person to a scheme's whole claims history. It is in the record under the patient's grant, and Money never holds it.

neverAccepts.refusal: A claim response may not carry a scheme's own words about a claim.
neverAccepts.why: A scheme's free text about why it did not pay is where a diagnosis is written down again. A decision is a code.

neverAccepts.refusal: A claim response may not carry an identity number.
neverAccepts.why: Money's claim reference is how an answer is matched. An identity number identifies nothing this door needs and cannot be changed when it leaks.

operator.section72: A claims switching house becomes an operator under POPIA section 21 on signature, and passes each claim to a medical scheme. Whether any of them processes a claim outside South Africa depends on a recipient nobody has named. Not determined.

feeds.name: Whether there will be power at the visit
feeds.supplier: EskomSePush, or Eskom's own status service, under a paid key. The free tier is licensed per person for non-commercial use, so a health service polling it is a breach rather than a bargain, and no key has been bought.
feeds.arrives: One zone's stage now, and the slots already scheduled for it. That is all: a fact about the grid, with no opinion about what should be done with it.

whileAbsent.unchanged: The board dispatches on roster, position and distance, and says nothing about power. A dispatcher who needs to know whether a zone is dark opens EskomSePush on her own phone, which is what she does today. Nothing here guesses a stage, and nothing here draws one.

accepts.why: One of the five zones geography.json already names — randburg, rosebank, parktown, melville, soweto. The vocabulary is this product's, not the supplier's: EskomSePush identifies a municipal area by its own id, and a feed that carried that id would put a second map of Johannesburg in the codebase, one nobody drew and one the dispatch board cannot join to anything.

The national stage the zone is under, 0 to 8. Zero is a reading and not an absence — the grid has held for months at a time — so a screen that renders zero as "no data" would be wrong on every one of those days, and would be wrong in the direction that makes a dispatcher think the board is broken rather than that the power is on.

The scheduled outage windows already published for that zone, each an ISO 8601 interval string. A list of strings because the contract takes no list of objects, and intervals because a slot is a span rather than a moment. Optional, because a stage with no published schedule is still a true statement about now, and refusing it would lose the one figure that is always available.

When the supplier read the grid, with an offset. A stage is a fact about a moment and it decays in an hour; a dispatcher who cannot see its age will plan an evening visit around a number that was true at lunchtime.

beforeSwitchOn.must: A paid EskomSePush key, or a written agreement with Eskom, covers commercial use by a health service, and the rate limit it comes with is recorded beside it.
beforeSwitchOn.why: The free tier is licensed per person and forbids commercial use. Polling it from a service is a licence breach dressed as a free integration, and the day it matters is the day the supplier notices — which is also the day a dispatch board loses the figure it was built around. The rate limit belongs in the same sentence because a key bought for a hobby cannot carry a fleet.

beforeSwitchOn.must: Every EskomSePush area id that maps onto a geography.json zone is recorded with the suburb list it was built from, and a person owns it.
beforeSwitchOn.why: EskomSePush names municipal areas; this product names five suburbs. The join between them is a judgement — Soweto sits across more than one Eskom area, and Randburg does not have the same edges in both — and a wrong join tells a dispatcher the power is on where it is off. That is the failure mode nobody would catch: the board looks authoritative, the nurse arrives in the dark.

beforeSwitchOn.must: No code derives a physical-or-virtual decision from this feed alone, and no screen presents a stage as a reason to defer a visit. The mode is a clinician's or a dispatcher's call, made with the visit in front of them, and an override is recorded against the person who made it.
beforeSwitchOn.why: This is the refusal that makes the feed safe to have. Load-shedding does not fall evenly: the stages are worst in the areas with the weakest infrastructure, which are the areas this product exists to serve. An engine that deferred a visit on "stage 6, no lighting" would defer it from Soweto and Alexandra and go ahead in Rosebank and Parktown, every day, by arithmetic — withdrawing physical care by postcode and calling it a safety feature. What a stage legitimately decides is whether a nurse can work safely and see, whether a device can be charged, and whether a call will drop mid-consultation. Those are operational facts for the person holding the roster, not a verdict on a patient.

beforeSwitchOn.must: observedAt is carried through to whatever renders the stage, and a reading older than the routing module's stale threshold is shown as stale rather than as current.
beforeSwitchOn.why: The same failure as a position with no clock, one subject away. Stages change with no notice and a stage that looks current is acted on.

neverAccepts.refusal: A load-shedding feed may not carry a patient id.
neverAccepts.why: The grid is a public fact about a suburb. Binding it to a person makes it a record that somebody who is ill lives somewhere without power — and that pair, held by a supplier, is a list of the patients least able to keep a device charged or keep food cold.

neverAccepts.refusal: A load-shedding feed may not name the visit.
neverAccepts.why: The same fact one indirection away: a visit reference resolves to a patient and an address for anybody holding both feeds, which is what nurse-position refuses for the same reason.

neverAccepts.refusal: A load-shedding feed may not carry an address or a coordinate.
neverAccepts.why: It answers for a zone and geography.json is explicit that a map here plots suburbs, not addresses. A coordinate in this feed would let a stage be joined to a doorstep, and the only reason to join them is the reason the zone exists to avoid.

neverAccepts.refusal: A load-shedding feed may not carry what a household has done about it.
neverAccepts.why: An inverter, a battery level, a meter reading: this is telemetry from inside somebody's home, arriving through the door that was opened for the national grid. It is also the sharpest possible inference — a household with no backup in a stage-6 zone is a household this product has just described as unable to keep medicine cold. The Devices engine has its own seam and its own DPIA; a grid feed is not the way in.

neverAccepts.refusal: A load-shedding feed may not carry a risk rating.
neverAccepts.why: The stage is what was measured. A risk level is somebody's conclusion about it, and it arrives looking like data — which is how a postcode ends up with a score attached that no clinician ever set and nobody can interrogate.

neverAccepts.refusal: A load-shedding feed may not carry a recommendation about how a visit should happen.
neverAccepts.why: Physical, virtual or deferred is the decision this feed must never make, and refusing it at the door is what keeps the switch-on condition true. A recommendation that arrives from a supplier is a decision taken by nobody in this country, about a named patient, with no clinician accountable for it and no override to record.

operator.section72: EskomSePush becomes an operator under POPIA section 21 on signature, and what it is sent is a list of the zones a nurse service operates in. Whether it processes anything outside South Africa depends on where a supplier nobody has named keeps its logs. Not determined.
